provenance: No value that existed in da0b593 has been changed by any amendment (amendments.json pins the hashes). Values added or moved into this file by amendments carry a `why...` note. The author did NOT re-derive the older values independently and does not claim a pre-registration; the review of every number by a reviewer who is not the author is requested before the next live result of the amended harness is accepted (docs/features/scene-acceptance.md, Provenance). A change after commit da0b593 is an amendment: amendments.json records the reason, the motivating finding and the SHA-256 of every pinned file before and after, and `tolerances_frozen` fails if a pinned file differs from the last recorded state.
units: pixels are 8-bit sRGB; positions are output pixels of the stated render size; audio is float PCM in [-1, 1]; times are seconds

camera.about: Markers are flat coloured quads (image planes) at known world positions. The model ray-casts the exact projected mask of each marker; the verifier measures the mask in the real picture from colour distance to the flat background. Position and shape are judged, never a probe lookup alone.

markerMask.why: marker and background colours differ by >= 120 on at least one channel; half of that is the edge threshold

camera.whyArea: A marker with fewer than 300 model pixels is clipped by the frame edge; its centroid and IoU move by the clipping, so it is not judged for position. One whose model area is 0 is outside the frame: it must leave at most 20 stray pixels (under 7% of the smallest judged mask; anti-aliasing of a neighbour can colour a few).

splat.about: Gaussian splats written by this corpus (SPZ v2) at known positions, colours, scales and opacities, drawn over a flat background plane. The model projects centre and size through the evaluated camera; the verifier measures centroid, centre colour, half-intensity radius and overlap order in the picture. Blending laws of the renderer are NOT modelled, only monotone quantities.

halfIntensityRadius.law: r50 = sigma * sqrt(2 ln 2) for an isotropic gaussian

splat.whyOverlap: Amendment A2. At the centre of the front splat the front colour is the picture (alpha 1). At the centre of the back splat the front gaussian is only partly opaque (alpha = exp(-d^2 / 2 sigma^2), 0.80 to 0.92 over the six frames), so the picture is the model's own over-composition (oracle.composite_at), judged within the same 40 the front rule always had; the >= 80 rule against the back colour is unchanged.
splat.opacityUnit: SPZ alpha byte / 255, applied once; an opaque (255) splat shows its colour at the centre

audio.channelLaw: The origin forces stereo (aformat channel_layouts=stereo) and sums with amix normalize=0, so FFmpeg's rematrix applies: mono -> stereo is 1/sqrt(2) per channel (-3.0103 dB), same layout is untouched. oracle.channel_gain_db; proof.spec.py re-derives it by running the origin's own filter.
audio.whyOnset: An edge is searched within 80 ms of the expected time (half a 24 fps frame is 21 ms, the AAC encoder delay about 21 ms) and is the first 1 ms RMS value reaching 35% of the expected tone RMS (the 2 ms window half-covers the edge at 50%).
audio.about: The oracle is analytic: a tone table, an exact rational frame-to-time mapping and a rate conversion that is the identity on the continuous signal. The exported file is decoded by ffmpeg to float PCM and compared with the analytic signal, never with a copy of the editor's mix.
negativeControlsMustFail: rate bug (44.1 kHz read as 48 kHz)
mono source written at 0 dB (channel law ignored)
retired A1 reading (mix[0] plays at editStartSeconds)

package.about: A package is judged by reading it with a reader that is not the editor's (Python zipfile / plain directory walk) and by what a restore recovers once the origin is deleted.
package.assetSha256: exact equality with the corpus hash, every asset, zero tolerance
negativeControlsMustFail: asset byte flipped inside the package
wrong hash declared in the bundle

export.about: Video timing and picture rules are inherited unchanged from scripts/directed-scene-export-proof (expected.json tolerances, fixed before any export existed); this harness adds no looser value.

blockedPolicy.rule: A phase whose dependency is absent (front S7 for splat in the directed scene, front S9 for mixed audio in the export) exits BLOCKED and the process exits 3 when nothing failed. BLOCKED is never counted as pass and never silently skipped, and it never replaces a FAIL: a phase that failed a check keeps FAIL even if a later step of it is blocked. Aceite of the integrated heads needs every phase to run and pass.

exit.0: every selected phase ran and passed
exit.1: at least one FAIL (also: the 2 GiB budget exceeded)
exit.2: harness usage error or prerequisite refused (disk reserve, stale binary) and no FAIL
exit.3: no FAIL but at least one BLOCKED
